description: Severity distribution for vehicle-pedestrian strikes, unmitigated (no barriers, speed controls, or high-vis). P(death) scale from AIS mortality data.
assumptions: No traffic barriers, speed humps, or exclusion zones
Vehicle mass typical for category (forklift 2-5t, car 1.5t, HGV 10-40t)

magnitude_bands.description: Yard/site speed. Forklift, reversing truck, construction vehicle manoeuvring. Includes crush/pin/run-over at very low speed.
magnitude_bands.mortality_source: NHTSA pedestrian impact data; forklift fatality data from OSHA/NIOSH. Forklift (2-5t at 10km/h) crush injuries are frequently fatal despite low speed.
magnitude_bands.rationale: Low speed but high mass — a forklift at walking pace still delivers enormous momentum. Crush/pin/run-over mechanisms dominate. Median is serious injury. P90 fatality from being pinned under vehicle or run over.

magnitude_bands.description: Urban/road speed. Car/van hitting pedestrian, HGV in work zone, site vehicle on access road.
magnitude_bands.mortality_source: Tefft 2013 (AAA Foundation): pedestrian fatality rate ~10% at 20mph, ~40% at 30mph, ~80% at 40mph. WHO pedestrian impact studies.
magnitude_bands.rationale: Tefft (2013) dose-response: pedestrian fatality risk increases steeply through this band. P50=0.50 reflects ~30-40% mortality midpoint. P10 reflects glancing blow at 20km/h.

magnitude_bands.description: Highway/dual carriageway speed (>60 km/h). Highway work zone, high-speed collision with pedestrian or cyclist.
magnitude_bands.mortality_source: Tefft 2013: >80% pedestrian fatality at 40mph+. DOT work zone fatality data.
magnitude_bands.rationale: At highway speeds, pedestrian survival is the exception. Published data shows >80% fatality rate above 60km/h. P10=serious_injury reflects rare glancing contact.

vehicle_mass.description: Multiplier on P(death). Heavier vehicles transfer more momentum. Forklift/PIT elevated above car because of crush/pin risk from low centre of gravity and forks.

victim_position.description: Multiplier on P(death). Prone/kneeling workers are at much higher risk of run-over. Elevated cab occupants partially protected.

sources.author: Tefft
sources.relevance: Impact speed and a pedestrian's risk of severe injury or death. AAA Foundation. Key dose-response for vehicle-pedestrian impacts.

sources.author: NHTSA
sources.relevance: Pedestrian safety data — speed vs fatality probability, impact biomechanics

sources.author: NIOSH
sources.relevance: Forklift-related fatalities — powered industrial truck struck-by data

sources.author: OSHA
sources.relevance: Focus Four: struck-by is #2 cause of construction fatalities after falls.

sources.author: Baker et al.
sources.relevance: AIS mortality rates — foundation for P(death) scale

validation_notes: STKY check: forklift strike should give P(SIF) > 0.50 — yard_speed P50=0.10, meets threshold ✓
STKY check: highway work zone strike should give P(SIF) near 1.0 — highway_speed, most outcomes serious+ ✓
Cross-check: Tefft 2013 is the definitive pedestrian dose-response — well-cited, used by NHTSA for policy
